findings.passage: Senate Bill 293, if signed into law by the Governor, will place new burdens on voters by adding unnecessary hurdles to the voting process and shortening the time available for Ohioans to make their voices heard.
findings.note: Her own newsletter section titled "SB 293 places New, Unnecessary Hurdles to Voting": criticizes ending the mail-ballot grace period and registration cancellations based on other agencies' databases. It adds: "It also creates vague and problematic procedures that could cancel registrations when other agencies' databases reflect different information or records, whether or not those records are factually correct."

findings.passage: We write to urge you to veto Substitute Senate Bill 293 which needlessly and recklessly changes Ohio voting laws to yet again add administrative barriers for Ohio citizens to cast their vote and have it counted. SB 293 eliminates the four-day grace period for timely mailed ballots to be received by Boards of Elections after election day and creates additional mechanisms to cancel voter registrations.
findings.note: Co-signed letter from House minority members to the Governor asking for a veto of SB 293 (mail-ballot receipt deadline and registration cancellation using other agencies' databases, which the bill ties to citizenship checks). Signed by Beryl Brown Piccolantonio (Minority Whip) with many colleagues; a shared statement, not written by this person alone.
